content.rendered: 2 years from now: We have ended our partnership with Kroger BMW, please enjoy your new Smartly Visa

I received Smartly Visa card a week ago which replaced my Harris Teeter MC. The card agreement wasn’t attached to the card and arrived separately this week. The agreement shows Foreign Transaction Fee is 0.00% for purchase or ATM advance in either US dollars or a Foreign Currency.

How’s everybody keeping the relationship open in between churns on the personal account? I just closed my personal checking, keeping my savings open, but now I see the savings has a $5 monthly fee.

Apparently the savings fee can only be waived with Smartly Checking, Smartly Visa CC, Smart Debit Account (which itself has a $4.95 fee), or if you’re under 18.

Should I close savings too and just keep a CD open indefinitely in between or something?

The 3% cash back card is not really completely unlimited because if you charge taxes or charge rent/mortgage, you get zero cash back. So, it’s just unlimited on any non-excluded categories. And of course, just like US Bank nerfed the 4% cash back Smartly Visa, a lot of folks think eventually there will be some nerfing of the X Money Card. Enjoy it and the extra interest boost while it lasts.
DP, USBANK smartly visa at Aldi was not paid, triggered by Target non groceries minutes prior going to Aldi…

mdacguy I am grandfathered, as you surmised.

I haven’t personally churned my U.S. Bank checking account, but I’d be cautious about closing the Smartly checking account if it is part of your Smartly Visa setup. Current public Smartly terms are very different from the original V1 setup as you are aware, and U.S. Bank’s current language appears to tie the earning bonus to having Smartly Savings plus qualifying balances in open Smartly Checking and/or Safe Debit accounts. DoC also reported that existing cardholders were split into different “good nerf” and “bad nerf” groups, with some still able to count investment balances and others not.

Because of that, I would not assume you can safely close the checking account, wait 12 months, reopen, and preserve the old investment-balance 4% treatment. Maybe it would be fine, but I personally would not risk a grandfathered 4% setup for a one-time checking bonus unless I had something in writing from U.S. Bank confirming that closing the checking account would not affect my Smartly Visa earning tier or grandfathered treatment.

Just purchased $200 card on US Bank Smartly Visa, sent to myself, and immediately received email with redemption instructions for both $200 and $40 card. Added to Lowes Wallet (which is hard to find on desktop (https://www.lowes.com/mylowes/profile/wallet/giftcards) without issue.

Giftcard has graphics that show “Homecare+” but is just a regular giftcard and fine print even says that. So if you send it to someone as a gift, they could confuse it as a giftcard for a Homecare+ subscription, which seems to be the intent of this marketing scheme.

Worked for me. Took a week to get approval, because I’d just opened the US Bank Checking for the bonus there. They eventually asked why I wanted to open Unitus in light of recently opening US Bank, and I told them I was disappointed about some of US Bank’s terms that I found out only after opening (which is true, I didn’t realize how nerfed the Smartly Visa was), and that I wanted a local CU (also true). They approved shortly after. No video call or anything beyond the initial e-mail.

The standard APY on the Smartly Savings account is 0.05%. For higher “relationship rates”, you’ll need a U.S. Bank Smartly Checking, Safe Debit account or Bank Smartly Visa Signature Card.

A Combined Qualifying Balance (CQB) of $25,000 and up could qualify you for an interest rate of up to 3.44% (3.50% APY). I use the word “could” because their website says “The displayed Annual Percentage Yield (APY) and interest rates are effective as of February 17, 2026 for ZIP code (my ZIP code) and are accurate for accounts opened on today’s date.” It also says “If you have an existing U.S. Bank Smartly Savings account, the advertised rates on this rate sheet may not apply. Log into your Online Banking or Mobile App to view your personalized account interest rate and interest rate bump or contact a banker.” Read more at USB: https://www.usbank.com/bank-accounts/savings-accounts/bank-smartly-savings/savings-account-interest-rates.html

If you don’t already have Smartly Checking, they do offer up to $450 SUB when you make qualifying deposits ($250 bonus for $3k deposits up to $450 bonus for $8k deposits). There’s another post here on DOC for the checking bonus: https://www.doctorofcredit.com/u-s-bank-450-100-checking-bonus/
Be aware the Smartly checking account has a $12 monthly fee, but there are several ways to get that fee waived.

Frank I called US Bank back later in the day. This second rep agreed with the first rep, but handed me off to a supervisor when I mentioned your comment, Frank. Supervisor said that the Smartly Visa card still is only available as metal, and that a replacement order will also be in metal. Also said 100% sure. And of course, this rep could also be misinformed, or the fact that plastic is now available is new, and has not been spread to the reps.
